policy_summary:
Confirmed by FOI: within the West Loch Lomond Camping Management Zone there are NO clearways on Argyll and Bute controlled roads, and NO provisions prohibiting overnight camping in lay-bys on their roads. Three of their off-street car parks sit inside the zone.

So on Argyll and Bute's roads inside the zone, staying overnight in a vehicle is lawful. The national park byelaw exempts vehicles on a road, and the council has added nothing on top.
notes:
An unusual record: the finding is an ABSENCE of restriction, confirmed in writing. That is worth as much to a user as a prohibition, and it is the kind of thing only an FOI produces - no council publishes a list of places it has not restricted.

The FOI dates from 2017, when the byelaws were being introduced. Needs re-checking, particularly with the ten-year review live.

OWN-PROVISION SWEEP, 27 July 2026 - NIL RETURN, AND THE NIL IS DELIBERATE. Country parks, council-owned caravan and camping sites, leased-out holiday parks, the Live Argyll leisure trust, the piers and harbours estate, the statutory asset register and the Rural Growth Deal were all checked. Argyll and Bute Council owns and runs NO campsite, caravan park, touring park or aire anywhere.

This is not an oversight, it is the council's stated position. Its own motorhome page says 'the council often does not own land in the areas where problems can occur and does not necessarily have the powers to address issues', and its aires page is written as advice TO private landowners and community groups on how to set one up themselves, complete with a support email address. The council is a facilitator that routes people to the Rural Tourism Infrastructure Fund. Compare Highland, which owns three caravan parks it never mentions - the difference between the two neighbouring councils is total.

LIVE ARGYLL, the council's arm's-length leisure trust, runs leisure centres, halls, libraries and museums and no accommodation of any kind. The Scottish leisure-trust pattern does not apply here.

THE HARBOURS ARE FOR BOATS, NOT VANS. The council owns around thirty piers, harbours and slipways. Campbeltown Harbour Marina, Rothesay Harbour (marina operated by Bute Berthing Company) and Oban North Pier Pontoons all sell overnight stays - to vessels. Oban's 'maximum of three nights' is a berthing limit. No council pier or harbour advertises overnight motorhome parking. Tobermory Harbour is a trust, Tarbert is a separate harbour authority and Ardrishaig is Scottish Canals, so none of those are the council's either.

One statutory trap worth recording: a caravan site occupied by the local authority is EXEMPT from caravan site licensing, so absence from the licence register is not by itself proof of nil provision. It is the council's own published statements, not the register, that carry this finding.

Private and third-sector supply named so nobody re-researches it: Argyll Caravan Park Inveraray, Lochgilphead Caravan Park, Rosneath Castle, Inverbeg, Ardlui, Drimsynie Estate Lochgoilhead, Hunters Quay Holiday Village, Point Sands Tayinloan, Carradale Bay, Kintra Farm Islay, Tralee Bay, North Ledaig, Sheiling Holiday Centre Benderloch and the Camping and Caravanning Club site at Gallanachmore, Oban. Forestry and Land Scotland's Argyll Forest Park 'Stay the Night' sites and the Loch Lomond and The Trossachs National Park Authority permit areas are separate register entries. The community-led Isle of Gigha motorhome and campsite is Isle of Gigha Heritage Trust, not the council.
open_questions: Re-confirm for 2026 - the FOI is nine years old and the byelaw review is in progress.
Which three off-street car parks inside the zone are theirs, and what are their rules?
Argyll and Bute is enormous and includes the west coast and the islands. Everything outside the Loch Lomond zone is unresearched.
Are there designated aires? Secondary sources mention some in Argyll and Bute without naming them.
Does any private caravan park in Argyll sit on council-owned land under lease? Lochgilphead Caravan Park and An Tairbeart at Tarbert could not be resolved either way.
The statutory register of land and assets could not be read end to end. The council warns it is incomplete, so a council-held caravan site could still be hiding in it.

sites.name: Argyll and Bute controlled roads and lay-bys, West Loch Lomond zone
sites.notes: Confirmed by FOI in 2017: no clearways, and nothing prohibiting overnight camping in lay-bys on their roads within the zone. Combined with the byelaw's road exemption, that makes overnight stays lawful here. Nine years old - re-check.

sites.name: Three Argyll and Bute off-street car parks inside the zone
sites.notes: Their existence is confirmed by FOI; their locations and rules are not. Off-street car parks are not covered by the byelaw's road exemption.
